requirements.title: Restore Ad Access on Original Account

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Hi [FREELANCER_NAME_001]
Before I hire you, I’d like to verify that you can assist with my specific problem.

My Meta ad account is [ACCOUNT_001] to run ads. Meta initially said 2FA was required, but two-step authentication is already enabled and verified on my personal account, and I have successfully run Facebook ads before.

Meta support now says the problem is connected to my personal Facebook profile rather than the ad account because of “account integrity/authentic identity.”

Have you previously resolved this exact kind of profile-level Meta restriction?

value_updates.expected_behavior: Restore the ability to run Facebook ads from the original account by resolving the profile-level account integrity or identity restriction.

execution.observed_behavior: The original Meta ad account cannot run ads because Meta associates the restriction with the client's personal Facebook profile.

source_message.speaker: freelancer
source_message.text:
Okay, I spoke to Meta Support, and they said that more than 180 days have passed since the user missed the deadline for restoring the ad account. Because of that, the restriction may be permanent.

However, the support team forwarded the case to their internal team and opened a support ticket. They will examine the account and confirm whether the restriction can still be removed or whether it is permanent.

I also asked about turning off Facebook's 2 factor authentication. They explained that, under Facebook's new "Advanced Protection" update, users can no longer completely disable 2 factor authentication after enabling it. This workaround worked previously, but because of security improvements, users are no longer able to fully turn off 2FA once it has been activated.

ambiguity.description: Meta support indicated that the expired appeal period may make the restriction permanent, while an internal review remained pending to determine whether recovery was still possible.

source_message.speaker: freelancer
source_message.text: They said that during the call. It can't be fixed because more than 180 days have passed. That is the appeal period.

execution.observed_behavior: Meta support reportedly concluded that the original account restriction could not be fixed because the 180-day appeal period had expired.
